PCC is a versatile technology that has been proven multiple times on a commercial scale and can be deployed in various industrial settings such as power generation facilities, steel fabrication mills, cement manufacturing, aluminum smelting, and more. As a result, PCC is an efficient and mature technology for greenhouse gas mitigation. The most well understood PCC technology is amine solvent-based carbon capture, which has been used in the gas sweetening industry for decades, with aqueous MEA being the industry standard solvent. MEA performance pales in comparison to next-generation CO capture solvents, which use much less energy, can 2 capture over 99% of CO in typical flue gas streams and are a critical technology to bridge the 2 energy demand gaps left by renewable energy sources. ION plans to deploy its transformational solvent-based CO capture technology as part of the effort to decarbonize the electrical grid and 2 minimize the effects of climate change. ION is currently in the process of scaling its second and third generation amine-based carbon capture solvents, ICE-21™ and ICE-31®, to the commercial level. In collaboration with Calpine, Sargent & Lundy, and Koch Modular Process Systems, ION has designed, constructed, and commissioned, a bespoke, 1 MWe (10 tonnes per day) CO capture 2 pilot plant at LMEC, NGCC power plant in Pittsburg, CA – “Project Enterprise” (ENTP).
